identity.operation: A finite command prefix can select either dump mode and carry nested JSON bytes. The entry calls json_loadb first, returns on NULL, and passes only its successful result to json_dumps or json_dump_callback.
identity.condition: An object with a child at dump depth JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH reaches do_dump's new failure guard when separately constructed, but JSON text that would yield such an object requires a parse_value call beyond the parser's maximum depth. json_loadb returns NULL before either dump call.
identity.capability: The JSON dump operation must be able to receive a supported, over-depth json_t so its clean depth-limit failure can be exercised.
identity.consequence: The JSON dump operation must be able to receive a supported, over-depth json_t so its clean depth-limit failure can be exercised.

obligations.requirement: The JSON dump operation must be able to receive a supported, over-depth json_t so its clean depth-limit failure can be exercised.

assessment.requirement: The JSON dump operation must be able to receive a supported, over-depth json_t so its clean depth-limit failure can be exercised.
assessment.target_route: A finite command prefix selects a dump mode and supplies JSON text. The entry passes the text to json_loadb, returns if loading fails, and passes only the loaded value to json_dumps or json_dump_callback.
assessment.failure_condition: A constructed nested value can reach do_dump at depth JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH and fail cleanly. JSON text yielding that child requires parse_value beyond JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH, so json_loadb returns NULL before dumping.
assessment.alternative_paths: JSON_DECODE_ANY changes the permitted root type and JSON_DISABLE_EOF_CHECK changes trailing-input handling; neither bypasses parse_value's depth check. Both dump modes use the same loaded value, and the complete entry has no later construction or mutation route.

necessity_evidence.reason: The dump API supports clean rejection of a constructed over-depth JSON value, but the target can dump only values accepted by its depth-limited loader. No input can deliver that value to either dump mode.

The loader rejects the text before dumping. A separately constructed nested array of that depth is the supported dump setup shown by the source test.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: json_dumps and json_dump_callback cleanly reject a constructed json_t whose child reaches JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH during dumping.
coverage_witness.required_setup: Construct a valid nested json_t deeper than JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH and pass it to a dump operation.
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: The entry creates its sole dump argument with json_loadb from input bytes and returns if loading yields NULL.
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: The parser rejects the nesting needed to reach the dump depth guard, preventing either dump mode from exercising its clean depth-limit failure.
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: Neither dump mode, load flag, nor later call sequence constructs or passes an over-depth object.
